questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Angle Between Two Vectors Given the Value of Their Dot Product
questions.problem: Given that $m\cdot n=10$, find the angle between $m=⟨t,-t,3⟩$ and $n=⟨3,2,4⟩.$ Round your answer to $2$ decimal places.
questions.worked_solution:
First, since $m\cdot n=10$, we can solve for $t$, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}m\cdot n & =10 \\ t\cdot 3+(-t)\cdot 2+3\cdot 4 & =10 \\ 3t-2t+12 & =10 \\ t & =-2\end{aligned}
$$

So, 

$$
\begin{aligned}m & =⟨(-2),-(-2),3⟩ \\  & =⟨-2,2,3⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the cosine of the angle between $m$ and $n$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =\frac{m\cdot n}{|\,m\,||\,n\,|} \\  & =\frac{{m}_{x}{n}_{x}+{m}_{y}{n}_{y}+{m}_{z}{n}_{z}}{\sqrt{{m}_{x}^{2}+{m}_{y}^{2}+{m}_{z}^{2}}\sqrt{{n}_{x}^{2}+{n}_{y}^{2}+{n}_{z}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{10}{\sqrt{(-2)^{2}+{2}^{2}+{3}^{2}}\sqrt{{3}^{2}+{2}^{2}+{4}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{10}{\sqrt{17}\cdot \sqrt{29}} \\  & =\frac{10}{\sqrt{493}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\theta =\operatorname{arccos}⁡(\frac{10}{\sqrt{493}})≈{63.23}^{∘}.
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Angle Between Two Vectors Given Three Points
questions.problem: Find $∠QPR$ given the points $P(2,1,2)$, $Q(1,3,2)$, and $R(4,5,-2).$ Round your answer to the nearest degree.
questions.worked_solution:
Note that the position vectors of the points $P$, $Q$, $R$ are

$$
\begin{aligned}p=⟨2,1,2⟩,\,q=⟨1,3,2⟩,\,r=⟨4,5,-2⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

The triangle $△PQR$ is shown (schematically) in the diagram below, where we denote $∠QPR=\theta .$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14071968/assets/3003f0cb329a8f8ef9bc315c70df4773ac1f0c54843dea1208c68bd0f6227bd1.png)

First, we find the components of $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ and $\overset{\to }{PR}$:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{PQ} & =q-p \\  & =⟨1,3,2⟩-⟨2,1,2⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,2,0⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{PR} & =r-p \\  & =⟨4,5,-2⟩-⟨2,1,2⟩ \\  & =⟨2,4,-4⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the cosine of the angle between $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ and $\overset{\to }{PR}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =\frac{\overset{\to }{PQ}\cdot \overset{\to }{PR}}{|\overset{\to }{PQ}||\overset{\to }{PR}|} \\  & =\frac{(-1)\cdot 2+2\cdot 4+0\cdot (-4)}{\sqrt{(-1)^{2}+{2}^{2}+{0}^{2}}\sqrt{{2}^{2}+{4}^{2}+(-4)^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{6}{\sqrt{5}\cdot \sqrt{36}} \\  & =\frac{6}{6\sqrt{5}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{5}}{5}\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence,

$$
\theta =\operatorname{arccos}⁡(\frac{\sqrt{5}}{5})≈{63}^{∘}.
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Angle Between Two Vectors Given Three Points
questions.worked_solution:
Note that the position vectors of the points $X$, $Y$, $Z$ are

$$
\begin{aligned}x=⟨-1,0,3⟩,\,y=⟨-2,2,3⟩,\,z=⟨-2,-1,3⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

The $△XYZ$ is shown (schematically) in the diagram below, where we denote $∠XZY=\theta .$ 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14071968/assets/87453fecb9da6b9e673ab5a85a289a3fac73f4fb90fc8f1b33e7c0a80b1ea77f.png)

First, we find the components of $\overset{\to }{ZX}$ and $\overset{\to }{ZY}$:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{ZX} & =x-z \\  & =⟨-1,0,3⟩-⟨-2,-1,3⟩ \\  & =⟨1,1,0⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{ZY} & =y-z \\  & =⟨-2,2,3⟩-⟨-2,-1,3⟩ \\  & =⟨0,3,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the cosine of the angle between $\overset{\to }{ZX}$ and $\overset{\to }{ZY}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =\frac{\overset{\to }{ZX}\cdot \overset{\to }{ZY}}{|\overset{\to }{ZX}||\overset{\to }{ZY}|} \\  & =\frac{1\cdot 0+1\cdot 3+0\cdot 0}{\sqrt{{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}+{0}^{2}}\sqrt{{0}^{2}+{3}^{2}+{0}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{3}{\sqrt{2}\cdot \sqrt{9}} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\theta =\operatorname{arccos}⁡(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}})={45}^{∘}.
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Angle Between Two Vectors Given Three Points
questions.worked_solution:
Note that the position vectors of the points $P,$ $Q$ and $R$ are

$$
\begin{aligned}p=⟨2,4,1⟩,\,q=⟨3,4,2⟩,\,r=⟨3,3,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

The triangle $△PQR$ is shown (schematically) in the diagram below, where we denote $∠QPR=\theta .$ 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14071968/assets/3003f0cb329a8f8ef9bc315c70df4773ac1f0c54843dea1208c68bd0f6227bd1.png)

First, we find the components of $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ and $\overset{\to }{PR}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{PQ} & =q-p \\  & =⟨3,4,2⟩-⟨2,4,1⟩ \\  & =⟨1,0,1⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{PR} & =r-p \\  & =⟨3,3,1⟩-⟨2,4,1⟩ \\  & =⟨1,-1,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the cosine of the angle between $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ and $\overset{\to }{PR}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =\frac{\overset{\to }{PQ}\cdot \overset{\to }{PR}}{|\overset{\to }{PQ}||\overset{\to }{PR}|} \\  & =\frac{1\cdot 1+0\cdot (-1)+1\cdot 0}{\sqrt{{1}^{2}+{0}^{2}+{1}^{2}}\cdot \sqrt{{1}^{2}+(-1)^{2}+{0}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}\cdot \sqrt{2}} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\theta =\operatorname{arccos}⁡(\frac{1}{2})={60}^{∘}.
$$

questions.problem: Given that $a\cdot b=-10$, find the angle between $a=⟨-4t,3t⟩$ and $b=⟨2,1⟩.$ Round your answer to $1$ decimal place.
questions.worked_solution:
First, since $a\cdot b=-10$, we can solve for $t$, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot b & =-10 \\ (-4t)\cdot 2+3t\cdot 1 & =-10 \\ -8t+3t & =-10 \\ -5t & =-10 \\ t & =2\end{aligned}
$$

So, 

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =⟨-4(2),\,3(2)⟩ \\  & =⟨-8,6⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the cosine of the angle between $a$ and $b$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =\frac{a\cdot b}{|\,a\,||\,b\,|} \\  & =\frac{{a}_{x}{b}_{x}+{a}_{y}{b}_{y}}{\sqrt{{a}_{x}^{2}+{a}_{y}^{2}}\sqrt{{b}_{x}^{2}+{b}_{y}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{-10}{\sqrt{(-8)^{2}+{6}^{2}}\sqrt{{2}^{2}+{1}^{2}}} \\  & =-\frac{10}{10\cdot \sqrt{5}} \\  & =-\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\theta =\operatorname{arccos}⁡(-\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}})≈{116.6}^{∘}.
$$
